_note: One entry per line that legitimately matches a public-surface rule, keyed by rule, file and the SHA-256 of the stripped line (so no matched text is stored here). Every entry needs a reason; an entry whose line no longer exists is a finding. Entries marked pending_owner_ruling are counted in the checker's output on every run.

entries.reason: Prose describing the defect that a sandbox path was once recorded in a provenance record; it quotes the shape of such a path, not a path of any machine.
A table row naming a gate and how many hard-coded developer paths it once found; it quotes the shape of the defect, not a path of any machine.
A comment recording that a committed record once carried a sandbox path; it quotes the shape of the path, not a real one.
The gate's docstring describing what it catches (a hard-coded developer or sandbox path).
The regular expression the gate uses to detect machine-specific paths; the line is the detector, not a path.
The gate's docstring describing what it catches (a hard-coded developer or sandbox path).
A regular expression the test uses to reject machine-specific paths in a provenance record; the line is the detector, not a path.
A phrase naming a simulation technique, in the audit's note about an undeclared dependency.
The word '<tool>' in an HTTP client's user-agent string, split across two lines of prose about identifying the client to a publisher.
The word '<tool>' in a comment about the HTTP client's default user-agent string, which a publisher's firewall may reject.
A local variable named for the HTTP user-agent string the client sends to a publisher; no assistant or product is named.
The name of an environment variable that the test asserts is ABSENT from the committed code (a list of forbidden names); it is checked for, not used.
